source_title: Hackers now scanning systems for recently-patched Oracle flaw
source_excerpt:
Attackers have begun probing the Internet for systems unpatched against a recently disclosed critical Oracle E-Business Suite (EBS) vulnerability.
Discovered in a core component of EBS's Application Object Library and tracked as CVE-2026-101767 , this flaw lets unauthenticated threat actors with HTTP network access take over vulnerable systems in low-complexity attacks.
Oracle released security updates to address the issue in its October 2026 Critical Security Patch Update on October 20 and urged customers to patch their systems immediately.
"In some instances, it has been reported that attackers have been successful because targeted customers had failed to apply available Oracle patches," it said. "Oracle therefore strongly recommends that customers remain on actively-supported versions and apply security patches without delay."
While Oracle has not yet tagged CVE-2026-101767 as exploited in the wild, threat intelligence company Defused said on Tuesday that it already spotted threat actors scanning the Internet for vulnerable systems.
"Our Oracle E-Business Suite decoys recorded exploratory exploits against CVE-2026-101767, an unauthenticated SQL injection in EBS's Thin Client Framework servlet that chains to remote code execution, this morning, Oct 27," Defused warned .
​Internet threat watchdog Shadowserver now tracks over 670 Internet-exposed Oracle EBS instances , most of them with IP addresses from the United States. However, Shadowserver doesn't indicate how many are honeypots or have already been secured against the CVE-2026-101767 flaw.
​Attackers often target Oracle vulnerabilities because they let them breach enterprise systems on the networks of many Fortune 100 corporations, government organizations, and healthcare networks around the world.
For instance, since early August 2025 , the Clop extortion gang has exploited another Oracle EBS flaw (CVE-2025-61882) in zero-day attacks targeting high-profile victims like Logitech , GlobalLogic , and the Washington Post , as well as US universities (including Harvard University , the University of Pennsylvania , Dartmouth College , and the University of Phoenix )
More recently, in June, Oracle released emergency mitigations for a critical PeopleSoft Suite zero-day (CVE-2026-35273) that the ShinyHunters extortion gang exploited between May 27 and June 9 .
By abusing this flaw, the threat actors gained unauthenticated remote code execution on victims' systems and stole data from many organizations worldwide, including Nottingham University , Nissan , and the National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC) .
Since November 2021, CISA has added 46 Oracle security bugs to its list of actively exploited vulnerabilities, 13 of which have also been abused in ransomware attacks.
